subject: SIG evidence: data decommissioning verification & forensic-hold gap analysis
messages:
From: Samantha Brooks <legal@heliahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <security@heliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: decommission verification + SIG/CAIQ artifacts for Helia retention carveout

Jonas —

Thanks for the run-through on Friday. As part of Helia's SIG review and our internal legal checklist, we need formal evidence that when tenant-level data is decommissioned (customer-initiated deletion or end-of-retention), Redwood performs the actions you describe in the SIG and CAIQ. Specifically we need:

- A short description of the decommission workflow (how and when snapshots are taken, which logs are preserved)
- Proof of deletion (audit entries / deletion receipts) for a sample recent tenant decommission
- How forensic holds/escrows are handled if a customer requests a temporary preservation outside the standard TTL
- Any known gaps where ephemeral caches (KV caches, short-lived inference artifacts) may not be captured by longer-term log exports

Can you provide these artifacts or point us to the records? We need to close this item for our board-reviewed compliance package by 11/10. If a side-channel call helps to agree the format, happy to schedule.

Best,
Samantha Brooks
Sr. Counsel, Helia Health
[sig-request-attachment: helia-questionnaire-20261101.pdf]

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Brooks <legal@heliahealth.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <security@heliahealth.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: decommission verification + SIG/CAIQ artifacts for Helia retention carveout

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Stephanie (INFRA/ops) and Olga (Security evidence) + Marcus (Product) to prepare a package. High-level answers up-front:

- Workflow: tenant decommission is a three-step pipeline: (1) customer API request -> tombstone marker in control plane, (2) async purge jobs sweep object storage + metadata indexes, (3) final audit record written and background erasure verified. Forensic holds convert tombstones to "preserve" state and trigger S3 object immutability snapshot + forensic snapshot of indexed logs.
- Proof of deletion: we have audit records in the control plane database (immutable append-only journal) and S3 object listing deltas; we can produce a redacted sample deletion receipt showing request id, operator id, and timestamp.
- Forensic holds: supported — legal hold request flips the deletion job to no-op and triggers a snapshot retained in our cold storage for up to the hold window requested. We can provide SOP + example evidence.
- KV / ephemeral caches: by design, inference KV caches and ephemeral process memory are not persisted to long-term logs. We do capture request/response metadata and token-level logs that allow reconstruction of interactions; we can document the residuals and their TTLs.

Action items:
1) Stephanie to produce the runbook + sample deletion receipt.
2) Olga to extract audit-journal snippets and the CAIQ/SIG references.
3) Marcus to confirm the product caveats on ephemeral caches and expected reconstruction limits.

We aim to deliver a packaged bundle and a short 30-minute walkthrough by 11/05. Does that timeline meet your 11/10 deadline?

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Security Eng, Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: decommission verification + SIG/CAIQ artifacts for Helia retention carveout

Jonas / team —

Attached are the items we can share as evidence (redacted where necessary):
- decommission-runbook.pdf (description of the three-step deletion pipeline, operator steps, and monitoring checks)
- log-preservation-sop.md (how we snapshot logs during a legal/forensic hold; includes retention mapping and who authorizes holds)
- forensics-snapshot-20261101.tar.gz (sample snapshot metadata only, no raw PII; manifests + checksums)

Notes and caveats (short):
- Deletion receipts: exported receipts contain request id, tenant id (redacted), timestamp, and final job status. We will remove tenant-specific PII before sharing.
- Ephemeral caches: these are in-memory only; we do not persist raw KV to blob stores, but we do persist service-level metadata and request tokens. That means perfect reconstruction is not guaranteed — we will add a short section called "reconstruction limitations" to the runbook.
- Timeline: Evidence bundle is attached and we can schedule a 30-min sync on 11/04 or 11/05 (I have availability 11/04 14:00-15:00 UTC).

Attachments: decommission-runbook.pdf; log-preservation-sop.md; forensics-snapshot-20261101.tar.gz

Thanks,
Stephanie
Infra Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — received the bundle and the caveats look reasonable. A couple of quick clarifying asks before we close the SIG item:

- Can you add a single-line attestation in the runbook indicating whether snapshots taken for legal hold are immutable (yes/no) and how immutability is enforced (object lock / WORM / access controls)?
- For the "reconstruction limitations" note: can you provide an example scenario (one short paragraph) showing what we would and wouldn't be able to reconstruct from the persisted telemetry?
- Please confirm how long the cold forensic snapshot is retained once a customer releases the hold (we need the retention end-to-end).

If you can reply by end-of-day Thursday (11/04) we'll mark the SIG question as satisfied. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Carlos
Head of InfoSec, Helia Health
